textual.observation: The ASR presents a Hashflare cloud-mining contract purchase, paid from an account balance, alongside a stated return of more than 200% per year.

evidence.quote: Choose payment method Pay by balance I confirm Confirm Yes Success Purchase was succesfull
The returns of the-Cash contract is more than 200% 200% PER YEAR

textual.context: The relationship is presented in first-person, participatory language; the ASR may contain transcription errors, and it is not clear from these records whether the statement is an endorsement, demonstration, or both.
textual.potential_relevance: A stated high return is directly connected in the same source to purchasing a mining contract and paying from a balance, so later review could assess the claim, its conditions, and whether the purchase depiction is promotional or demonstrative.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish that the return was achieved, guaranteed, typical, available to viewers, or accurately transcribed; they also do not establish the identity or legitimacy of the service, any actual financial loss, or the outcome of the depicted purchase.

visual.observation: Frames F0041 and F0047 show a Russian-language cryptocurrency cloud-mining interface with one-year X11 (DASH) and Equihash (ZEC) options, selectable hash-rate amounts, an apparent USD-denominated amount, a green “Дальше” (“Next”) button, and a “Прогноз доходности” (“profitability forecast”) panel with ZEC/USD outputs.
visual.context: The man appears in a picture-in-picture window while the mining interface is displayed; it is unclear from these frames whether the segment is promoting, reviewing, warning about, or demonstrating the service.
visual.potential_relevance: A cryptocurrency profitability forecast is visibly presented in connection with selecting a paid one-year mining plan and proceeding via the “Next” control, creating a task-relevant reward/return-to-payment/action relationship that conditionally merits review.
visual.limitations: These sampled frames do not establish that any payment, account creation, transfer, mining activity, promised return, or transaction outcome occurred; they also do not show the full terms or whether the forecast was presented as guaranteed.

textual_context_notes.observation: The speaker uses repeated buying language and describes having money for Hashflare, supporting a promotional or participatory framing, although the precise intent is unclear from ASR alone.

The interface visibly shows “0 H/s,” “0 ZEC = 0.00 USD,” and text indicating that pool settings will be available on a later date.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes Hashflare cloud-mining contracts through a referral URL, showing paid one-year Equihash options and a purchase process. It ties a claimed return of more than 200% per year to the same Zcash contract purchase, although the evidence does not establish that the returns were achieved or guaranteed.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The displayed paid hashpower selection and the speaker's reported balance-funded contract purchase are linked to his claim of annual returns from that contract. The return is a speaker claim, not a verified payout or guarantee.
